docs.title: from_network(net, *, cost='length', **kwargs) classmethod
docs.text:
Build a graph from a :class:netstead.network.Network (corral package).

Materializes the node and link tables to pandas and delegates to :meth:build. cost defaults to "length" so distance-based ops (:meth:network_buffer) and connectivity work without extra arguments.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default net Network

docs.title: netstead.clean.simplify_geometry(net, session, *, mode='redundant_only', tolerance=0.0)
docs.text:
Drop redundant interior vertices on every link geometry.

The shapes are edited where they live: on link.geometry when the link table carries geometry inline, otherwise on the geometry table that link.geometry_id points at (inline wins when both exist). The returned edit — and its rollback — target that table, so a network that keeps shapes in geometry never grows an inline column as a side effect.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default net Network

The source :class:Network. Must carry link shapes either as an inline link.geometry column or in a geometry table.

required session Session

An open :class:corral.editing.Session bound to net. The returned :class:EditResult is appended to the session’s log so :meth:Session.rollback can undo it.

required mode str

"redundant_only" (default) drops vertices that are collinear with their neighbours within tolerance. No spatial accuracy is lost when tolerance == 0.0. "douglas_peucker" runs shapely’s :meth:shapely.geometry.LineString.simplify with the given tolerance (CRS units).

'redundant_only' tolerance float

Threshold in CRS units. For redundant_only this is the maximum perpendicular distance a vertex can sit from the chord through its neighbours before it is considered non-redundant. For douglas_peucker it is the shapely tolerance.

0.0

Returns:

Name Type Description An EditResult EditResult

edit; result.edit.table is "link" or "geometry"

EditResult

depending on where the shapes live.

Raises:

Type Description CleanError

If the network has no link shapes in either location, or mode is unrecognized.

Examples:

>>> import pytest
>>> _ = pytest.importorskip("shapely")
>>> from netstead import Network
>>> from corral.editing import Session
>>> # (See packages/netstead/tests/test_clean.py for runnable examples.)
>>> simplify_geometry

docs.text:
Resolve a single finding to its “Edit in OSM” deep link, or None.

Resolution order, first match wins:

  1. issue.extra["osm_way_id"] / ["osm_node_id"] / ["osm_relation_id"] — fast-path for callers (quality rules, custom checks) that already know the OSM provenance and stash it on the issue.
  2. issue.table == "link" + issue.row → look up the row in network.links and read its osm_way_id column.
  3. issue.table == "node" + issue.row → look up the row in network.nodes and read its osm_node_id column (only set on OSM-sourced networks).

Returns None for any finding whose network has no OSM provenance columns, and for any finding whose row lookup yields a missing / NaN OSM id.

required network Network

docs.text:
The parser that select.provider / select.model describe.

model=None means the provider’s default, from :meth:~netstead.llm.registry.ProviderRegistry.resolve_model: the catalog default, or for Ollama an installed tool-capable model when the catalog default isn’t installed.

When the catalog knows model and lists tools = false (e.g. a model whose docs say tool/function calling isn’t available), the parser starts in JSON mode instead of attempting a forced tool call first. A model the catalog doesn’t know (custom endpoint, or an Ollama-discovered tag) keeps today’s behavior: try tools, then fall back to JSON mode on :class:~netstead.llm.errors.ToolsUnsupported.

docs.title: netstead.select.resolve
docs.text:
Resolve a SelectionIntent to GMNS link/node ids against a network.

ProjectCard-select-links parity. Pipeline (engine-agnostic; pandas frames): 1. base selection — link_ids | select_all | facility (name/ref, any class) 2. direction filter — facility bearing within +-75 deg of the cardinal 3. modes/conditions — AND-filters on link attributes 4. segment or whole — if from/to anchors: shortest path along the facility (freeway gore/merge, or at-grade intersections); else the whole filtered set. Names match exactly, then by spelling, direction or a close misspelling (:class:~netstead.select.streets.StreetIndex). A partly-freeway facility (a trunk road with signals) that has no interchange path tries its at-grade intersections, and a street whose own name breaks off (a nameless roundabout, a median crossing) is bridged by short links.

CSS height for the map <div>. Inline-styled so a host page can size embeds independently.

'480px' uid str | None

Stable identifier for the instance. Auto-generated if not provided. Useful to pin in tests or to deep-link to a specific embed on a multi-map page.

None

Examples:

Standalone single-file HTML::

>>> from netstead import Network
>>> from netstead.fixtures import leavenworth
>>> from corral.engines.ibis_engine import IbisEngine
>>> from netstead.map import NetworkMap
>>> net = Network.from_source(leavenworth.csv_dir(), engine=IbisEngine())
>>> html = NetworkMap(net, title="Leavenworth").to_html()
>>> html.lstrip().startswith("<!DOCTYPE html>")
True

Compose two maps in one custom page::

>>> a = NetworkMap(net, uid="left", title="Left").body_fragment()
>>> b = NetworkMap(net, uid="right", title="Right").body_fragment()
>>> head = NetworkMap.head_assets()
>>> page = f"<!DOCTYPE html><html><head>{head}</head><body>{a}{b}</body></html>"
>>> 'gv-map-left' in page and 'gv-map-right' in page
True

Bind the network + optional issue overlay to a fresh NetworkMap instance.

docs.text:
Shared CSS + JS for any number of :class:NetworkMap instances.

Returns an HTML string containing the inlined Leaflet CSS+JS, water.css baseline, our component CSS, and the :func:window.__netsteadAttach definition + queue drainer. Include ONCE in the host page’s <head>; idempotent if included multiple times.

The string contains <style> and <script> blocks — drop it verbatim. No remote references; the report works offline.

Place this anywhere on the host page. Multiple instances can coexist — each carries its own UID and its own payload slot in window.__NETSTEAD_INSTANCES__.

Also carries row_props for row-level findings (link / node tables) so the findings-table “Fix locally” action can open the same mini-editor the marker popup uses — without duplicating the lookup on the JS side.

docs.title: netstead.map.render_validation_html(network, report, **opts)
docs.text:
Render a validation report page: NetworkMap + findings table.

Equivalent to::

m = NetworkMap(network, issues=report.issues, **opts)
# ...then composed with a findings table around it.

The findings table chrome (severity chips, filter bar, the issue rows themselves, the “unlocated findings” block) is rendered in :file:templates/validation_report.html.j2 — see there for the structure. The map fragment is dropped in via :meth:NetworkMap.body_fragment so the same component you embed elsewhere (notebook, custom page) is the one in the report.

Two things keep a partial package’s report readable (2026-10-20 beta feedback): a “Resources” table built from :func:corral.reports.grouping.resource_inventory says which spec tables are present instead of one finding per absent table, and the collapsed “Unlocated findings” block folds structural findings that differ only by resource into one line (:func:corral.reports.grouping.group_issues). The source path is printed once, in the subtitle; the package source '…': lead-in is stripped from every message.

docs.title: netstead.workbench.actions.BaseAction
docs.text:
Bases: BaseModel

Base class for every Workbench Action, core and plugin.

A subclass declares type: Literal["<type>"] = "<type>" (plugins: "<plugin id>.<name>") and its fields. mutates marks actions the assistant must draft before applying; runs_as_job (core only) runs the slow work on a background job thread; replay_overrides are fields forced in the to_python replay snippet, and replay_omits are fields it leaves out (a guard that only means something in the live session, such as a planned version). assistant = False keeps an Action out of the natural-language assistant’s tools, even when its plugin is opted in (Host API 1.4). assistant_compact = True offers a mutates Action in the assistant’s compact tool set too (assistant.compact_tools, on for a model on this machine): that set keeps the read-only Actions and only the mutating ones so marked (Host API 1.6).

Field values must round-trip through repr (str, numbers, bools, None, lists/dicts/tuples of those, nested pydantic models): “copy session as Python” writes each field as name=<repr(value)>, so a value whose repr isn’t valid Python makes the copied script fail.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
netstead is the command-line front door to the library: inspect, validate, convert, build, scope, clean and benchmark GMNS networks, and start the HTTP, MCP and Workbench servers. The command tree below is generated from the live typer app (netstead.cli.app) on every docs build, so it cannot drift from the installed version; netstead --help and netstead <command> --help print the same text in the terminal.

Three conventions apply across the tree:

  • --json. Every data command accepts --json and then writes exactly one JSON document to stdout, so the result pipes into jq or straight into an agent. The index table marks which commands take it.
  • netstead doctor is an install doctor: Python version, optional extras, vendored spec versions, and whether the bundled Leavenworth fixture loads. To diagnose a network, use netstead validate (spec, schema and foreign-key checks) or netstead quality (data-quality rules).
  • Optional extras. Commands that need an extra (server, mcp, clean, osm, reports, …) are always listed in --help. When the extra is missing they exit with code 1 and one line on stderr, netstead.<module> requires the [<extra>] extra: pip install 'netstead[<extra>]', which names the extra to install; netstead doctor shows which extras are present.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Usage: netstead [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

Options

Option Type Default Help --install-completion flag Install completion for the current shell. --show-completion flag Show completion for the current shell, to copy it or customize the installation. Command What it does --json netstead validate Validate source against the GMNS spec. yes netstead info Print GMNS-aware metadata about source — spec version + table summary. yes netstead convert Convert a data package from any supported format to another. yes netstead quality Run the GMNS data-quality rule pack against source. yes netstead doctor Check your netstead install — Python version, extras, vendored specs. yes netstead bench Run read/validate/connectivity benchmarks; print timings. yes netstead bench-suite Run the DuckDB-path benchmark suite (create / selection / viz-pack). netstead build Build a GMNS network from OpenStreetMap or Overture and write it to DEST. yes netstead select Resolve a natural-language selection to GMNS link/node ids. yes netstead select-serve Serve the interactive selection map: now an alias of netstead app SOURCE. netstead viz Serve the network viewer: now an alias of netstead app SOURCE. netstead app Serve the Netstead Workbench: open, inspect, and select on GMNS networks in the browser. netstead spec GMNS spec utilities — list and diff vendored versions. per sub-command netstead server Run the netstead self-hostable HTTP server. per sub-command netstead mcp Run the netstead MCP server for AI-agent access. per sub-command netstead clean GMNS network-editing ops (requires the ‘clean’ extra). per sub-command netstead scope Build a NetworkScope and print its (links, nodes) sets. per sub-command netstead index Spatial + graph index build/status/drop. per sub-command netstead llm Language-model providers for natural-language features. per sub-command

docs.title: netstead validate
docs.text:
Validate source against the GMNS spec.

Runs the four-pass validator (structural / schema / foreign-key / sync-state) with the GMNS spec auto-loaded — so reading a CSV directory without a datapackage.json gets the real per-table schema checks, not the empty “every table is unexpected” output of the generic corral validate.

Exit code is non-zero iff any ERROR-severity issue is recorded.

Examples: Validate the bundled Leavenworth fixture as CSVs::

        $ netstead validate path/to/leavenworth/csv

    Write the interactive map+table HTML viewer::

        $ netstead validate path/to/network --html report.html

    Export findings to a spreadsheet::

        $ netstead validate path/to/network --csv f.csv --xlsx f.xlsx

Usage: netstead validate [OPTIONS] SOURCE

Arguments

Argument Type Required Help SOURCE path yes Path / URL to a GMNS network (datapackage.json or CSV/Parquet/DuckDB directory).

Options

Option Type Default Help --spec text Override the default GMNS spec version (e.g. ‘0.96’). Defaults to netstead.DEFAULT_SPEC. --json flag Emit JSON on stdout instead of rich panels. --all flag List every finding on its own row instead of folding repeated structural findings into one. --html path Write the interactive network-on-map HTML viewer to this path. Falls back to a table-only HTML report when the [reports] extra is not installed. --csv path Write the flat findings table to this CSV path. --xlsx path Write the flat findings table to this XLSX path (requires [reports] extra). --yes, -y flag Auto-approve any gated ops (alternative to CORRAL_AUTO_APPROVE=1).

Machine-readable: --json writes the result to stdout as JSON.

docs.title: netstead convert
docs.text:
Convert a data package from any supported format to another.

Loads source (any format corral can read) and writes the same logical package to dest in the target format. Output format is taken from --format when supplied, otherwise inferred from the dest extension; an extension-less dest defaults to partitioned parquet (architecture §6.1).

Usage: netstead convert [OPTIONS] SOURCE DEST

Arguments

Options

Option Type Default Help --format, -f text Output format (csv/parquet/duckdb/zipcsv). Default: infer from dest extension; fall back to parquet. --engine text Engine: DuckDB (the only compute engine). --json flag Emit JSON on stdout. --yes, -y flag Auto-approve gated ops.

Machine-readable: --json writes the result to stdout as JSON.

Run the GMNS data-quality rule pack against source.

Arguments

docs.title: netstead doctor
docs.text:
Check your netstead install — Python version, extras, vendored specs.

This is an INSTALL doctor, not a network doctor. To diagnose a
specific GMNS network, use:

  netstead validate <path>    spec / schema / FK / sync-state checks
  netstead quality  <path>    data-quality rules (high speed on residential, etc.)
  netstead info     <path>    table list + row counts

Exits non-zero on any install failure.

Options

Machine-readable: --json writes the result to stdout as JSON.

docs.title: netstead bench
docs.text:
Run read/validate/connectivity benchmarks; print timings.

Phases timed (each via time.perf_counter):

  • load — Network.from_source.
  • validate — Network.validate (structural/schema only).
  • links_count + nodes_count — trivial materialization sanity.
  • is_connected — full graph index build + component count (skipped silently when the [graph] extra is missing).

Output is a dict with phases (list of {phase, seconds}) and a total_seconds summary. --json writes the dict to stdout for machine consumption; otherwise rendered via the standard rich panel.

Usage: netstead bench [OPTIONS] SOURCE

Arguments

Argument Type Required Help SOURCE path yes Path/URL to a GMNS network.

Options

Option Type Default Help --engine text Compute engine (DuckDB is the only one; kept for compatibility). --json flag Emit JSON on stdout.

Machine-readable: --json writes the result to stdout as JSON.

docs.title: netstead bench-suite
docs.text:
Run the DuckDB-path benchmark suite (create / selection / viz-pack).

Sweeps the requested size tiers over the three operation families from the benchmarking-suite scope, capturing wall-time and peak memory, and emits one structured document. DuckDB (via ibis) is the single compute engine; pandas / polars / pyarrow are I/O formats, so there is no engine axis — the suite measures the DuckDB path and the binary store format.

--format json (default) emits the canonical regression document; csv flattens the results; md renders the advertising table with an environment stamp and the standing honesty caveats. Fixture definitions live in benchmarks/fixtures.toml; the L tier is resolved from the NETSTEAD_BENCH_LARGE / NETSTEAD_BENCH_LARGE_BBOX env vars (never committed).

Usage: netstead bench-suite [OPTIONS]

Options

Option Type Default Help --sizes text S,M Size tiers to sweep (comma-separated: S,M,L). --operations text network_create,selection,viz_pack Operation families to run (comma-separated). --format text json Output format: json | csv | md. --output, -o path Write to this file instead of stdout. --repeats integer 3 Macro timing repeats (reported as median + min). --warm-repeats integer 20 Repeats for the warm selection number. --run-osm flag Include live OSM builds (hits Overpass). --fixtures path Override path to a fixtures.toml. --commit text Git SHA to stamp into the env block.

docs.title: netstead select
docs.text:
Resolve a natural-language selection to GMNS link/node ids.

Prints the validated selection fragment on success (exit 0). On an ambiguous result it prints the status, the provisional link ids, each anchor with the other nodes it could be, and diagnostics (exit 3); on not-found it prints diagnostics (exit 1).

With a language model chosen and select.grammar_first on (the default), the offline grammar is tried first and the model is called only when it can’t read the request with names the network has, as in the Workbench.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Two sections: GMNS domain terms come from the spec itself and apply to any GMNS toolkit. Project conventions are Netstead + corral specific — names that appear in the API, CLI, and docs of this toolkit. Entries are alphabetical within each section.

docs.title: GMNS domain
docs.text:
Allowed uses — the set of uses permitted to traverse a link or lane (e.g., auto, truck, transit). Encoded as a comma-separated string on link.allowed_uses / lane.allowed_uses whose members name a use_definition.use or a use_group.use_group (a use_group row lists its members in its own comma-separated uses field). GMNS 0.97 has no prohibited_uses field. See use_definition.

Capacity — the maximum hourly throughput of a link or lane under prevailing conditions, in vehicles per hour. Carried on link.capacity (and overridable per period via link_tod.capacity). Units are vehicles per hour per lane unless the producer notes otherwise; GMNS is silent on the LOS model used to compute it.

Curb segment — a managed length of curb (parking, loading zone, no-stopping). One row per curb segment in curb_seg, keyed to a link_id. New in recent GMNS versions; supports curb-management modeling.

Facility type — descriptor of a link’s roadway class (e.g., motorway, primary, tertiary, residential, service). In GMNS 0.97 link.facility_type is free text — the spec does not enumerate it (shared_categories.json only defines barrier, bike_facility, ped_facility, parking categories, movement_type and ctrl_type). The quality rule pack reads it by name (e.g. residential for the high-speed-residential rule).

Free speed — the posted or signed speed limit, or the speed at which vehicles travel under uncongested conditions. Carried on link.free_speed; the unit is network-wide, declared in config.speed (usually long_length units per hour), not per link. Distinct from any modeled travel speed.

Geometry — a row in the optional geometry table holding a WKT LineString, referenced by link.geometry_id. When absent, the link is implicit straight-line from from_node to to_node. The geometry table exists so multiple links can share one shape (e.g., a divided highway represented as two opposing links sharing a centerline).

GMNS — General Modeling Network Specification. The Zephyr Foundation’s open standard for routable transportation networks in tabular Frictionless Data Package form. See What is GMNS?.

Lane — a sub-element of a link with its own lane number, optional turn restrictions, and allowed uses. One row per travel lane per link in the lane table; lane.lane_id is the primary key and lane.link_id is the foreign key to link.link_id. A link with lanes=3 typically has three corresponding lane rows.

Link — a directed edge in the routable network, from from_node_id to to_node_id. The required spine table; carries facility type, lanes, free speed, length, allowed uses. Undirected networks are represented by paired links (one per direction).

Movement — a turning movement at a node, from an inbound link to an outbound link. One row per allowed turn in the movement table; carries movement type (left/through/right/u-turn) and permitted uses. Used by signal-control tables to map phases to movements.

Node — a vertex in the routable network — intersection, dead-end, zone centroid. The required vertices table; carries x/y coordinates and optional ctrl_type (signal, stop, yield, no-control).

Segment — a sub-division of a link where attributes change mid-link (e.g., a lane drop, a facility-type change). One row per segment in the segment table; segments tile a link end-to-end. Used when link-level attributes are too coarse.

Spec version — the GMNS spec release the data conforms to. Netstead vendors 0.95, 0.96, and 0.97. Validation reports always include the spec version. The default is 0.97; override via Network.from_source(path, spec_version="0.96").

TOD (time-of-day) — per-time-period overrides on link / lane / segment / movement attributes. Keyed by timeday_id into time_set_definitions. A period like weekday_am_peak (Mon-Fri 07:00-09:00) is defined once and referenced from every *_tod row that varies by that period.

Zone — a traffic analysis zone (TAZ) for demand modeling. Nodes carry an optional zone_id. The zone table holds polygon or centroid geometry; not every network has zones (routing-only networks often don’t).

docs.title: Project conventions
docs.text:
ApprovalRequired — exception raised when a gated operation’s cost estimate exceeds the approval threshold (default 180 seconds) and the caller has not set approve=True. See the cost-model section of Architecture.

Auto-build threshold — the network size (in nodes) above which a netstead.scope op logs an INFO message when it has to build the scipy graph index on first call (the build happens either way; the threshold only controls the log). Default 50,000 nodes. Configurable via the NETSTEAD_AUTO_INDEX_THRESHOLD environment variable. Pre-build explicitly with net.build_indexes(graph=True) to control timing.

CORRAL_AUTO_APPROVE — environment variable (CORRAL_AUTO_APPROVE=1) that bypasses the cost-model approval prompt for gated operations. Equivalent to CLI --yes or programmatic approve=True. Intended for batch / CI use.

EditResult — the value returned by every netstead.clean op. Carries the diff per affected table, the log entry for the operation, and a _repr_html_ visual summary for notebook rendering. Integrated with corral.editing.Session for rollback.

Engine — the compute backend. corral has one: IbisEngine (lazy expressions over DuckDB). pandas / polars / pyarrow are I/O formats (.to_pandas() / .to_polars()), not compute engines. See corral.engines.

NETSTEAD_AUTO_INDEX_THRESHOLD — see Auto-build threshold.

Lazy expression — a Table.expr that has not been materialized. Operations on a lazy expression return a new lazy expression. Materialization happens explicitly via .to_pandas(), .to_polars(), .collect(), .head(), or .count().

MCP (Model Context Protocol) — the open protocol Claude and other AI agents use to discover and call tools. Netstead ships an MCP server via pip install 'netstead[mcp,graph]'; start it with netstead mcp serve. Tools exposed: describe_package, validate_package, list_tables, describe_network, quality_check, connected_components, scope_from_nodes — all stateless, each taking a source. See the MCP tools reference and Architecture §6.9.

Network buffer — a Dijkstra-bounded expansion in graph distance (using link.length). Used by netstead.scope.from_node(id, network_buffer="200m"). Distinct from spatial buffer.

OutOfSyncWarning — warning raised before write() or validate(strict=True) when any tracked foreign-key’s source or target table hash has changed since the last validation. Indicates the in-memory FK graph may no longer match the data. Promote to an error with strict=True.

Scope — a NetworkScope is a (node_ids, link_ids) pair that, when applied via .apply(), returns a filtered Network with every other table pre-filtered by FK chain. Scopes are composable and chainable: net.scope.from_nodes([1,2,3]).buffer_network("0.5mi").buffer_spatial(30). See Architecture §6.2.

Session — corral.editing.Session, a context manager around one or more EditResults with atomic rollback. Open with with Session(net, log_path=...) as s: ...; s.rollback() (no arguments) reverses every edit of the open session in LIFO order. The parquet log is written on clean exit only when log_path= is given; corral.editing.rollback(pkg, log_path, to=session_id_or_datetime) replays that log later to reverse edits selectively. (The Workbench’s netstead.workbench.Session is a different class — the action bus of the local web app.)

Severity / Category / Issue — see the corral API reference. Severity is one of ERROR, WARNING, INFO (serialized lower-case). Category discriminates rule families: SCHEMA, STRUCTURAL, FOREIGN_KEY, SYNC_STATE, DATA_QUALITY — a quality finding carries DATA_QUALITY plus one of the three severities. Issue is the per-finding record carried in a ValidationReport.

Skill (Claude Code Skill) — a packaged set of instructions and prompts a Claude Code agent can load on demand. Netstead ships six (gmns-author, gmns-build, gmns-validate, gmns-convert, gmns-clean, corral-validate) under skills/ in the repo. Install with claude code skill add <git-url>#path=skills/<name>. See Architecture §6.9.

Spatial buffer — a shapely-bounded expansion in CRS units (degrees for WGS84, meters for projected CRSs). Used by netstead.scope.from_link(id, spatial_buffer_m=...) and the buffer_spatial() chain method. Distinct from network buffer.

Sync state — content-hash tracking on every table via DirtyTracker (in corral.validation.sync_state). Records source + target hashes per FK at validation time so the validator can detect when a previously-checked FK has gone stale. Direct DataFrame mutations bypass the tracker — call net.invalidate("link") to force.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
netstead.config.Settings is the one model behind the Workbench’s Settings dialog, the netstead app flags, SetSetting actions and the config files. It has twelve typed sections (io, engine, osm, overture, build, validation, select, llm, assistant, viz, app, credentials) plus a free-form plugins table. Every section rejects unknown keys (extra="forbid"), so a typo in a file is an error, not a silently ignored line.

The tables below are generated from the pydantic model: field names, types and defaults are the model’s own. The “Applies” column says when a change takes effect in a running Workbench: live means the next action reads the new value; next launch means the server reads it only when netstead app starts (these four keys are tagged applies on next launch in the Settings dialog, and a session-scope change to them does nothing).

docs.title: Where settings come from
docs.text:
Precedence, lowest to highest — a later layer overrides the earlier ones key by key:

  1. Model defaults (the tables below).
  2. User file: ~/.config/netstead/config.toml ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/netstead/config.toml when set; %APPDATA%\netstead\config.toml on Windows; NETSTEAD_CONFIG_DIR overrides the directory).
  3. Project file: ./netstead.toml in the current directory (or the project_dir passed to load_settings / Session).
  4. Environment variables NETSTEAD_<SECTION>__<FIELD>.
  5. Session overrides: CLI flags (netstead app --port 9100), Session(overrides={...}), and SetSetting(scope="session").

load_settings() records which layer each leaf value came from; the Settings dialog shows that as a badge (default, user, project, env, session). Load the layers and read where a value came from:

from netstead.config import get_value, load_settings

loaded = load_settings(environ={"NETSTEAD_VIZ__BASEMAP": "esri"}, overrides={"app.port": 9100})
print(loaded.settings.viz.basemap, loaded.sources["viz.basemap"])
print(get_value(loaded.settings, "app.port"), loaded.sources["app.port"])
print(loaded.sources["io.spec_version"])

Expected:

esri env
9100 session
default

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: The name is NETSTEAD_ + the dotted key upper-cased with __ for each dot: NETSTEAD_APP__PORT=9100, NETSTEAD_LLM__OLLAMA__BASE_URL=http://gpu-box:11434, NETSTEAD_IO__ALLOWED_ROOTS='["/data/networks"]'. A value starting with [ or { is parsed as JSON (that is how lists and tables are passed); anything else is a string that pydantic coerces to the field’s type. An env value outranks both files, and the Settings dialog says so when a saved value would not take effect.

docs.title: TOML files
docs.text:
Both files use the same shape — one table per section, nested tables for llm.<provider>, llm.quality, validation.rules.<code> and plugins.<id>:

# ./netstead.toml
[app]
port = 8900

[viz]
basemap = "esri"

[select]
provider = "ollama"

[llm.ollama]
base_url = "http://localhost:11434"

[validation.rules."quality.high_speed_residential"]
enabled = true
severity_override = "info"
thresholds = { max_free_speed = 45 }

save_setting(key, value, scope="user" | "project") writes one dotted key into the chosen file (and value=None removes it); the Workbench’s Save to picker calls the same function.

docs.title: Secrets are never settings
docs.text:
API keys, tokens and passwords are refused everywhere settings are written:

  • SetSetting refuses, before anything is recorded, a key or value that looks like an API key, a key whose last segment is secret-shaped (*_key, token, password, …), any URL carrying user:password@, and a base_url with a query string or fragment.
  • [plugins.<id>] tables are free-form, so the model applies the same secret-name check to them in every layer — files and env included — and a hit fails validation with the key named, never the value.
  • llm.* holds endpoints only; keys go through the Workbench’s write-only key route or netstead llm set-key into the OS keyring. credentials.keyring_hosts names hosts, never what is stored for them.
  • io.allowed_roots is config-only: the action API refuses to change it at any scope (a file, an env var or the command line can widen the sandbox; an action cannot).

A single name is accepted; the old drive reads as roads and walk, bike, all as both. live build.buffer_m float (> 0) 1000.0 Buffer in metres the wizard prefills for a point area. live build.extra_tags list[str] [] Extra OSM tags the wizard prefills. live

docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning Applies validation.rules dict[str, RuleSettings] {} One table per rule code (e.g. quality.high_speed_residential). live (next validation)

Each RuleSettings value has enabled: bool = true, severity_override: "error" | "warning" | "info" | None = None and thresholds: dict = {} (the rule’s own threshold names). A code no installed rule has is reported as unknown by the validation result, not refused.

docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning Applies select.provider "stub" \| "anthropic" \| "openai" \| "gemini" \| "ollama" "stub" Which provider parses utterances (stub is the offline pattern parser). The old name claude is accepted and stored as anthropic. live select.model str \| None None Model name (None: the provider’s catalog default; for Ollama, an installed tool-capable model). live select.grammar_first bool true Read a request with the offline pattern parser first and call the model only when that reading names a street, route number or road type the network doesn’t have, or selects nothing. Ask does the same with the offline assistant (streets and columns must be in the network). false sends every request to the model. live

docs.text:
llm.anthropic, llm.openai and llm.gemini share one shape; llm.ollama has local defaults.

Key Type Default Meaning Applies llm.anthropic.base_url str \| None None Endpoint override (None: the official endpoint). Must be http(s), no userinfo, query or fragment. live llm.anthropic.timeout_s float (0 < x ≤ 600) 60.0 Whole-request timeout. live llm.openai.base_url str \| None None As above (any OpenAI-compatible server). live llm.openai.timeout_s float (0 < x ≤ 600) 60.0 As above. live llm.gemini.base_url str \| None None As above. live llm.gemini.timeout_s float (0 < x ≤ 600) 60.0 As above. live llm.ollama.base_url str \| None "http://localhost:11434" The Ollama server. A non-local URL means utterances leave this machine. live llm.ollama.timeout_s float (0 < x ≤ 600) 120.0 Whole-request timeout. live

llm.quality controls what the natural-language features send and how hard they try. "auto" means on for a local endpoint (Ollama, or any loopback base_url) and off for a remote provider.

Key Type Default Meaning Applies llm.quality.assistant_context bool true Send the shipped GMNS assistant notes (gmns_assistant.md) as context. live llm.quality.assistant_context_max_chars int (0–100000) 16000 Cap on those notes. live llm.quality.project_context "auto" \| "on" \| "off" "auto" Send the project’s AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md. live llm.quality.project_context_max_chars int (0–50000) 4000 Cap on the project notes. live llm.quality.grounding "auto" \| "on" \| "off" "auto" Send network vocabulary (street names, route numbers) to the model. live llm.quality.grounding_max_names int (1–2000) 200 How many names grounding sends. live llm.quality.few_shot bool false Add this session’s resolved selections as examples (same network only; never persisted). live llm.quality.few_shot_max int (1–10) 3 How many examples. live llm.quality.max_repairs int (0–5) 1 Re-prompts after an invalid tool call. live llm.quality.temperature float \| None (0–2) 0.0 Sampling temperature (None: the provider’s default). live llm.quality.match_retry "auto" \| "on" \| "off" "auto" After a miss, re-prompt with only the closest real names (a bool is accepted: true → on). live llm.quality.match_candidates int (1–20) 5 How many candidate names that retry sends. live

docs.title: [assistant] — the natural-language assistant
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning Applies assistant.actions list[str] the 14 default action types (see below) Core Actions the assistant may call. Opt-ins: add_rows, set_setting, build_network, delete_selection. open_network / close_network are never offered. live assistant.plugins list[str] [] Plugin ids whose Actions it may call. live assistant.max_steps int (1–20) 6 Tool calls per question. live assistant.history_turns int (0–20) 6 Past turns sent with each question. live assistant.max_turns int (1–500) 50 Turns kept in the conversation. live assistant.output_token_limit int (128–8192) 1024 Output tokens per model call. live assistant.context_max_chars int (1000–100000) 12000 Cap on the session state sent (grounded extras give way first). live assistant.remote_token_budget int (0–10000000) 200000 Tokens a remote provider may spend this session before the assistant stops. live assistant.compact_tools "auto" \| "on" \| "off" "auto" Offer a small model fewer tools per question (auto: on for a local endpoint). live

The default assistant.actions list is select, clear_selection, pin_anchor, save_selection, use_selection, style, filter, navigate, set_active_network, run_validation, edit_cells, delete_rows, undo_edit, save_network (netstead.config.DEFAULT_ASSISTANT_ACTIONS). It uses select.provider / select.model and the llm.quality privacy gates.

For example, the bundled project-cards plugin reads [plugins.project_cards]:

docs.title: Official GMNS Specification
docs.text:
The GMNS specification is managed in the following Github repo: https://github.com/zephyr-data-specs/GMNS

This page renders the upstream master branch of that repository at docs build time: the macro fetches Specification_md/datapackage.json from GitHub and tabulates each resource and its schema. When the fetch fails (offline build, GitHub unreachable) it logs a warning and falls back to the vendored 0.97 spec at packages/netstead/netstead/spec/0.97/, so the tables below may be the vendored copy rather than the live branch.

GMNS Version Description development Not yet in official spec. Hasn’t been voted on by PMG local Local copy of spec. May not be identical to official spec.

GMNS is defined using the Frictionless Framework as a series of tabular-data-resources.

docs.title: Files in Specification
docs.text:
GMNS consists of a package of files as defined in the following table.

The following tables are automatically generated from the official spec.

docs.title: General Modeling Network Specification (GMNS)
docs.text:
Name: gmns Version: 0.96 Homepage: https://github.com/zephyr-data-specs/GMNS

The General Modeling Network Specification (GMNS) defines a common machine (and human) readable format for sharing routable road network files. It is designed to be used in multi-modal static and dynamic transportation planning and operations models.

docs.title: link
docs.text:
A link is an edge in a network, defined by the nodes it travels from and to. It may have associated geometry information. Links have three types of attributes: - Those that define the physical location of the link (e.g., shape information, length, width) - Those that define the link’s directionality: from_node, to_node - Those that define properties in the direction of travel: capacity, free flow speed, number of lanes, permitted uses, grade, facility type

Primary key: link_id

Field Type Constraints Description link_id any required Primary key - could be SharedStreets Reference ID name string Optional. Street or Path Name from_node_id any required Required. Origin Node to_node_id any required Required. Destination Node directed boolean required Required. Whether the link is directed (travel only occurs from the from_node to the to_node) or undirected. geometry_id any Optional. Foreign key (Link_Geometry table). geometry any Optional. Link geometry, in well-known text (WKT) format. Optionally, other formats supported by geopandas (GeoJSON, PostGIS) may be used if specified in geometry_field_format in gmns.spec.json parent_link_id any Optional. The parent of this link. For example,for a sidewalk, this is the adjacent road. dir_flag integer enum=[1, -1, 0] Optional. 1 shapepoints go from from_node to to_node;-1 shapepoints go in the reverse direction;0 link is undirected or no geometry information is provided. length number min=0 Optional. Length of the link in long_length units grade number min=-100; max=100 % grade, negative is downhill facility_type string Facility type (e.g., freeway, arterial, etc.) capacity number min=0 Optional. Saturation capacity (passenger car equivalents / hr / lane) free_speed number min=0; max=200 Optional. Free flow speed, units defined by config file lanes integer min=0 Optional. Number of permanent lanes (not including turn pockets) in the direction of travel open to motor vehicles. It does not include bike lanes, shoulders or parking lanes. bike_facility string enum=[unseparated bike lane, buffered bike lane, separated bike lane, counter-flow bike lane, paved shoulder, shared lane, … (+4 more)] Optional. Type of bike facility along the link. ped_facility string enum=[unknown, none, shoulder, sidewalk, offstreet_path, crosswalk] Optional. Type of pedestrian accommodation along the link parking string enum=[unknown, none, parallel, angle, other] Optional. Type of parking along the link. allowed_uses string Optional. Set of allowed uses that should appear in either the use_definition or use_group tables; comma-separated. toll number Optional. Toll on the link, in currency units. jurisdiction string Optional. Owner/operator of the link. row_width number min=0 Optional. Width (short_length units) of the entire right-of-way (both directions).

Foreign keys:

  • from_node_id → node.node_id
  • to_node_id → node.node_id
  • geometry_id → geometry.geometry_id
  • parent_link_id → link.link_id

docs.title: node
docs.text:
A list of vertices that locate points on a map. Typically, they will represent intersections, but may also represent other points, such as a transition between divided and undivided highway. Nodes are the endpoints of a link (as opposed to the other type of vertex, location, which is used to represent points along a link)

Primary key: node_id

Field Type Constraints Description node_id any required Primary key name string x_coord number required Coordinate system specified in config file (longitude, UTM-easting etc.) y_coord number required Coordinate system specified in config file (latitude, UTM-northing etc.) z_coord number Optional. Altitude in short_length units. node_type string Optional. What it represents (intersection, transit station, park & ride). ctrl_type string enum=[no_control, yield, stop, stop_2_way, stop_4_way, signal_with_RTOR, … (+1 more)] Optional. Intersection control type. zone_id any Optional. Could be a Transportation Analysis Zone (TAZ) or city, or census tract, or census block. parent_node_id any Optional. Associated node. For example, if this node is a sidewalk, a parent_nodek_id could represent the intersection it is associated with.

Foreign keys:

  • zone_id → zone.zone_id
  • parent_node_id → node.node_id

docs.title: geometry
docs.text:
The geometry is an optional file that contains geometry information (shapepoints) for a line object. It is similar to Geometries in the SharedStreets reference system. The specification also allows for geometry information to be stored directly on the link table.

Primary key: geometry_id

Field Type Constraints Description geometry_id any required Primary key - could be SharedStreets Geometry ID geometry any Link geometry, in well-known text (WKT) format. Optionally, other formats supported by geopandas (GeoJSON, PostGIS) may be used if specified in geometry_field_format in gmns.spec.json.

docs.title: lane
docs.text:
The lane file allocates portions of the physical right-of-way that might be used for travel. It might be a travel lane, bike lane, or a parking lane. Lanes only are included in directed links; undirected links are assumed to have no lane controls or directionality. If a lane is added, dropped, or changes properties along the link, those changes are recorded on the segment_link table. Lanes are numbered sequentially, starting at either the centerline (two-way street) or the left shoulder (one-way street or divided highway with two centerlines).

Primary key: lane_id

Field Type Constraints Description lane_id any required Primary key link_id any required Required. Foreign key to link table. lane_num integer required; min=-10; max=10 Required. e.g., -1, 1, 2 (use left-to-right numbering). By convention, the left-most through lane is 1. Left-turn lanes have negative numbers allowed_uses string Optional. Set of allowed uses that should appear in either the use_definition or use_group tables; comma-separated. r_barrier string enum=[none, regulatory, physical] Optional. Whether a barrier exists to prevent vehicles from changing lanes to the right. l_barrier string enum=[none, regulatory, physical] Optional. Whether a barrier exists to prevent vehicles from changing lanes to the left width number min=0 Optional. Width of the lane, short_length units.

Foreign keys:

  • link_id → link.link_id

Primary key: link_tod_id

Foreign key to time_set_definitions. time_day string Conditionally required (either timeday_id or time_day). XXXXXXXX_HHMM_HHMM, where XXXXXXXX is a bitmap of days of the week, Sunday-Saturday, Holiday. The HHMM are the start and end times. capacity number min=0 Optional.Saturation capacity (pce / hr / lane) free_speed number min=0; max=200 Optional. Free flow speed in long_distance units per hour lanes integer min=0 Optional. Number of permanent lanes (not including turn pockets) in the direction of travel open to motor vehicles. It does not include bike lanes, shoulders or parking lanes. bike_facility string enum=[unseparated bike lane, buffered bike lane, separated bike lane, counter-flow bike lane, paved shoulder, shared lane, … (+4 more)] Optional. Type of bike facility along the link. ped_facility string enum=[unknown, none, shoulder, sidewalk, offstreet_path, crosswalk] Optional. Type of pedestrian accommodation along the link parking string enum=[unknown, none, parallel, angle, other] Optional. Type of parking along the link. allowed_uses string Optional. Set of allowed uses that should appear in either the use_definition or use_group tables; comma-separated. toll number toll in currency units.

  • timeday_id → time_set_definitions.timeday_id

docs.title: location
docs.text:
A location is a vertex that is associated with a specific location along a link. Locations may be used to represent places where activities occur (e.g., driveways and bus stops). Its attributes are nearly the same as those for a node, except that the location includes an associated link and node, with location specified as distance along the link from the node.

Primary key: loc_id

Field Type Constraints Description loc_id any required Primary key. Location ID. link_id any required Required. Road Link ID. Foreign Key from Road_Link. ref_node_id any required Required. The From node of the link. Foreign Key from Node. lr number required; min=0 Required. Linear Reference of the location, measured as distance in short_length units along the link from the reference node. If link_geometry exists, it is used. Otherwise, link geometry is assumed to be a crow-fly distance from A node to B node. x_coord number Optional. Either provided, or derived from Link, Ref_Node and LR. y_coord number Optional. Either provided, or derived from Link, Ref_Node and LR. z_coord number Optional. Altitude in short_length units. loc_type string Optional. What it represents (driveway, bus stop, etc.) OpenStreetMap map feature names are recommended. zone_id any Optional. Foreign Key, Associated zone gtfs_stop_id string Optional. Foreign Key to GTFS data. For bus stops and transit station entrances, provides a link to the General Transit Feed Specification.

Foreign keys:

  • link_id → link.link_id
  • ref_node_id → node.node_id

docs.title: movement
docs.text:
Describes how inbound and outbound links connect at an intersection.

Primary key: mvmt_id

Field Type Constraints Description mvmt_id any required Primary key. node_id any required The node representing the junction. name string Optional. ib_link_id any required Inbound link id. start_ib_lane integer Innermost lane number the movement applies to at the inbound end. end_ib_lane integer Outermost lane number the movement applies to at the inbound end. Blank indicates a movement with a single inbound lane. ob_link_id any required Outbound link id. start_ob_lane integer Innermost lane number the movement applies to at the outbound end. end_ob_lane integer Outermost lane number the movement applies to at the outbound end. Blank indicates a movement with a single outbound lane. type string enum=[left, right, uturn, thru, merge, diverge] Optional. Describes the type of movement (left, right, thru, etc.). penalty number Turn penalty (seconds) capacity number Saturation capacity in passenger car equivalents per hour. ctrl_type string enum=[no_control, yield, stop, stop_2_way, stop_4_way, signal_with_RTOR, … (+1 more)] Optional. mvmt_code string pattern=^[NSEW][EWB][RLT]\d?$ Optional. Movement code (e.g., SBL). Syntax is DDTN, where DD is the direction (e.g., SB, NB, EB, WB, NE, NW, SE, SW). T is the turning movement (e.g., R, L, T) and N is an optional turning movement number (e.g., distinguishing between bearing right and a sharp right at a 6-way intersection) allowed_uses string Optional. Set of allowed uses that should appear in either the use_definition or use_group tables; comma-separated. geometry any Optional. Movement geometry, in well-known text (WKT) format. Optionally, other formats supported by geopandas (GeoJSON, PostGIS) may be used if specified in geometry_field_format in gmns.spec.json

docs.title: use_definition
docs.text:
The Use_Definition file defines the characteristics of each vehicle type or non-travel purpose (e.g., a shoulder or parking lane). A two-way left turn lane (TWLTL) is also a use.

Primary key: use

Field Type Constraints Description use_group string required Primary key. uses string required Comma-separated list of uses. description string Optional.

docs.title: time_set_definitions
docs.text:
The time_set_definitions file is an optional representation of time-of-day and day-of-week sets to enable time restrictions through _tod files.

Field Type Constraints Description timeday_id any required Primary key.Primary key, similar to service_id in GTFS. Unique name of the time of day. Preferable legible rather than a number. monday boolean required Required. Whether Mondays are included. tuesday boolean required Required. Whether Tuesdays are included. wednesday boolean required Required. Whether Wednesdays are included. thursday boolean required Required. Whether Thursdays are included. Friday boolean required Required. Whether Fridays are included. saturday boolean required Required. Whether Saturdays are included. sunday boolean required Required. Whether Sundays are included. holiday boolean required Required. Whether holidays are included. start_time time required Required. Start time in HH:MM format. end_time time required Required. docs.title: segment
docs.text:
A portion of a link defined by link_id,ref_node_id, start_lr, and end_lr. Values in the segment will override they value specified in the link table. When one segment is fully contained within another, its value prevails.

Primary key: segment_id

Field Type Constraints Description segment_id any required Primary key. link_id any required Required. Foreign key to road_links. The link that the segment is located on. ref_node_id any required Required. Foreign key to node where distance is 0. start_lr number required; min=0 Required. Distance from ref_node_id in short_length units. end_lr number required; min=0 Required. Distance from ref_node_idin short_length units. grade number min=-100; max=100 % grade, negative is downhill capacity number min=0 Optional. Saturation capacity (pce/hr/ln) free_speed number min=0; max=200 Optional. Free flow speed, units defined by config file lanes integer Optional. docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
GMNS 0.97 defines 25 resource files grouped into four families: required, detail, signal-control, and dimension. Two tables (link, node) are required by the spec; the rest layer optional detail. This page is the “which table should I use?” entry point. For field-level detail (types, constraints, descriptions per column) see Schema reference.

The vendored 0.97 spec lives at packages/netstead/netstead/spec/0.97/. Each table is defined by a <name>.schema.json and listed as a resource in datapackage.json.

docs.title: Required
docs.text:
These two tables form the routable graph spine. A valid GMNS package must include both.

Table Purpose Key foreign keys link Directed edges of the routable graph; one row per road segment between two intersections. Carries facility type, lane count, free-flow speed, allowed uses. from_node_id, to_node_id → node.node_id; geometry_id → geometry.geometry_id (optional); parent_link_id → link.link_id (self-ref, optional) node Vertices of the routable graph; intersections, dead-ends, zone centroids. Carries x/y coordinates and control type. zone_id → zone.zone_id (optional); parent_node_id → node.node_id (self-ref, optional)

docs.title: Detail tables
docs.text:
Add geometric, lane-level, segment-level, or curb-level detail to the link/node spine. All optional.

Table Purpose Key foreign keys lane One row per travel lane on a link. Carries lane number, width, allowed uses, turn restrictions. link_id → link.link_id segment Sub-divides a link where attributes change mid-link (e.g., a lane drop). One row per segment. link_id → link.link_id; ref_node_id → node.node_id segment_lane One row per lane within a segment. Same role as lane but at segment granularity. segment_id → segment.segment_id link_tod Time-of-day override on link attributes (capacity, allowed uses) for a defined period. link_id → link.link_id; timeday_id → time_set_definitions.timeday_id lane_tod Time-of-day override on lane attributes. lane_id → lane.lane_id; timeday_id → time_set_definitions.timeday_id segment_tod Time-of-day override on segment attributes. segment_id → segment.segment_id; timeday_id → time_set_definitions.timeday_id segment_lane_tod Time-of-day override on segment-lane attributes. segment_lane_id → segment_lane.segment_lane_id; timeday_id → time_set_definitions.timeday_id movement A turning movement at a node, from an inbound link to an outbound link. Carries permitted uses and a movement type (left/through/right/u-turn). node_id → node.node_id; ib_link_id, ob_link_id → link.link_id movement_tod Time-of-day override on movement attributes. mvmt_id → movement.mvmt_id; timeday_id → time_set_definitions.timeday_id; ib_link_id, ob_link_id → link.link_id geometry WKT LineString per link. Referenced by link.geometry_id; optional (links can be implicit straight from-to). (primary key; referenced by link) zone Traffic analysis zone (TAZ) polygons or centroids for demand modeling. super_zone → zone.zone_id (self-ref, optional); referenced by node.zone_id location Curb-side point of interest — a stop, a pick-up location, a service door. link_id → link.link_id; ref_node_id → node.node_id (zone_id is a plain column, not a declared FK) curb_seg A managed curb segment with allowed uses, parking regulations, loading-zone designations. link_id → link.link_id; ref_node_id → node.node_id

docs.title: Signal-control tables
docs.text:
Carry signalized-intersection timing and detection data. All optional; needed only when modeling signal operations.

Table Purpose Key foreign keys signal_controller One row per signal controller (typically one per signalized intersection). (primary key controller_id; no foreign keys — the controller is placed by the tables that reference it) signal_coordination Coordination relationships between controllers in a corridor. timing_plan_id → signal_timing_plan.timing_plan_id; controller_id, coord_contr_id → signal_controller.controller_id signal_detector Detector loops / video zones on link approaches. controller_id → signal_controller.controller_id; link_id → link.link_id; ref_node_id → node.node_id signal_phase_mvmt Maps movements to signal phases (which phase serves which turning movement). timing_phase_id → signal_timing_phase.timing_phase_id; mvmt_id → movement.mvmt_id; link_id → link.link_id signal_timing_phase Per-phase timing parameters (min green, max green, yellow, all-red). timing_plan_id → signal_timing_plan.timing_plan_id signal_timing_plan A named timing plan (cycle length, offset, plan identifier) for one controller. controller_id → signal_controller.controller_id; timeday_id → time_set_definitions.timeday_id (when plan is TOD-bound)

docs.title: Dimension tables
docs.text:
Vocabularies and configuration referenced by the detail and signal-control tables. All optional but typically present when any TOD or use-restriction is used.

Table Purpose Key foreign keys time_set_definitions Named time periods (e.g., weekday_am_peak = Mon-Fri 07:00-09:00). Referenced by every *_tod table. (primary key) use_definition A defined vehicle / mode class (auto, truck, transit, bike, walk). (primary key use; named by use_group.uses and the allowed_uses columns, which are comma-separated text, not declared FKs) use_group A named set of use_definition members (e.g., motorized = {auto, truck, transit}). (primary key use_group; members listed in its uses text field — no declared foreign key) config One row of network-wide configuration columns (dataset_name, length and speed units, crs, geometry_field_format, currency, version_number, id_type). (no primary key, no foreign keys)

docs.text:

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Every state change in a Workbench session — a click in the browser, a line of Python, a step the assistant drafts — is one typed Action: a pydantic model in netstead.workbench.actions, discriminated on its type string. The session validates the Action, applies it under its lock, records a HistoryEntry and publishes the new state. Because the vocabulary is the same everywhere, anything the UI did can be copied as Python and replayed.

This page lists the 21 core Actions in netstead.workbench.actions.CORE_ACTIONS (plugins register more). For each: the fields with their types and defaults (a field with no default is required), the class flags, and the snippet to_python writes for it. The flags are class attributes:

  • mutates — the assistant must draft the Action and get approval before applying it; it also marks what undo and rollback care about.
  • runs as job — the slow work runs on a background job thread; Session.dispatch waits for it, Session.submit returns the Job.
  • replay — what the “copy as Python” snippet does with the fields: fields equal to their default are omitted; replay_omits fields are left out (expected_version, a guard that only means something in the live session); replay_overrides are forced (BuildNetwork always replays with approved=True).

All 21 core Actions have assistant = True, the class flag that lets an Action be offered to the natural-language assistant at all. The flag matters for plugin Actions: a plugin that is opted in through assistant.plugins can still keep one of its Actions out of the assistant’s tools by setting assistant = False on that class. Which core Actions the assistant may call is a setting, assistant.actions (14 by default; open_network and close_network are never offered) — see the Settings reference.

docs.title: OpenNetwork — open_network
docs.text:
Load a GMNS network from a local path (inside io.allowed_roots) or URL and make it active. Runs as a job (open <name>); does not mutate. Result: {"net_id": ...}.

Field Type Default source str required label str \| None None net_id str \| None None (derived from the source)

Replay: app.do(OpenNetwork(source='/data/net', label='Leavenworth'))

docs.text:

Field Type Default net_id str required

Replay: app.do(CloseNetwork(net_id='leavenworth'))

docs.text:

docs.title: Select, pin, save, use, delete selection
Select — select
docs.text:
Select features by natural-language utterance or explicit ids. Give exactly one of utterance or link_ids. query is the parsed intent for utterance (the selection tool’s arguments); with it no parser runs, so a replay is exact — the assistant records its selections this way.

Replay: app.do(PinAnchor(role='to', node_id=60))

docs.text:

docs.title: Style — style
docs.text:
Partially update the map style; omitted fields are unchanged. color_by colors links by a column of the link table and node_color_by colors nodes by one of the node table ("none" for a single color); width_by sizes links by a numeric column ("none" for widths by lane count). A fresh session defaults color_by to "facility_type" and node_color_by to "ctrl_type" when those columns exist ("none" otherwise).

Field Type Default color_by str \| None None node_color_by str \| None None width_by str \| None None ramp "YlOrRd" \| "Blues" \| "Viridis" \| None None show dict[("links" \| "nodes" \| "labels" \| "selection"), bool] \| None None colors dict[("links" \| "nodes" \| "selection"), [r, g, b]] \| None None offset bool \| None None show_direction bool \| None None show_legend bool \| None None

Replay: app.do(Style(width_by='lanes'))

docs.title: Filter — filter
docs.text:
Show only the links matching every condition; the map dims the rest and the table’s Filtered scope lists them. A constrained predicate over link columns, never SQL. where=None (or an empty list) clears the filter; at most MAX_FILTER_CONDITIONS conditions.

Field Type Default net_id str \| None None where list[FilterCond] \| None None

A FilterCond is {col: str, op: FilterOp, val} with op one of eq ne lt lte gt gte in contains isnull notnull any_of all_of none_of between; in takes a list, isnull / notnull take no value. The token operators any_of / all_of / none_of match a list of values against a comma-separated cell such as allowed_uses ("auto" matches "auto,truck,walk"; a bare value is read as a one-element list; an empty cell matches only none_of). between takes [low, high], inclusive.

Replay: app.do(Filter(where=[{'col': 'lanes', 'op': 'gte', 'val': 2}]))

docs.text:

A replayed save writes the copy again, so it fails with “already exists” while the earlier copy is there.

docs.title: From Python
docs.text:
netstead.workbench.Session is the action bus. Construct one (it loads settings from the usual layers; overrides is the session layer), dispatch Actions with session.dispatch(...) — session.do is the same method, which is why copied snippets read app.do(...) — and read session.history, a list of HistoryEntry records each carrying the Action as JSON, its python replay snippet, ok, result and any error.

The fixture folder is passed as an allowed root because a Session built from Python only trusts the folders in io.allowed_roots:

from netstead.fixtures import leavenworth
from netstead.workbench import Filter, OpenNetwork, Select, Session, Style

source = str(leavenworth.csv_dir())
app = Session(overrides={"io.allowed_roots": [source]})

print(app.do(OpenNetwork(source=source, label="Leavenworth")))
selection = app.do(Select(link_ids=[1, 2, 3]))
print(selection["status"], selection["link_ids"])
app.do(Style(width_by="lanes"))
app.do(Filter(where=[{"col": "lanes", "op": "gte", "val": 2}]))

for entry in app.history:
    print(entry.seq, entry.ok, entry.python)

Expected:

{'net_id': 'leavenworth'}
resolved [1, 2, 3]
1 True app.do(OpenNetwork(source='...
2 True app.do(Select(link_ids=[1, 2, 3]))
3 True app.do(Style(width_by='lanes'))
4 True app.do(Filter(where=[{'col': 'lanes', 'op': 'gte', 'val': 2}]))

Three details worth knowing:

  • dispatch raises the recorded failure’s type — ApprovalRequired (with .estimate), PathNotAllowed, NotSupportedYet, JobCancelled, else ActionError. dispatch_recorded returns the HistoryEntry instead and never raises ActionError.
  • A dict is accepted in place of a model: app.do({"type": "style", "width_by": "lanes"}) is parsed through the session’s registry (session.actions), which also knows plugin Actions. netstead.workbench.actions.parse_action parses core Actions only.
  • Session.add_network(net) registers an already-loaded Network without an Action, so it is not in the history and a copied script does not replay it.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
netstead app serves one Workbench Session as a local web app. The browser front end is only a client of the routes below; anything it does, a script can do with curl or an HTTP library. The route list is generated on every docs build from the FastAPI app’s OpenAPI document (build_app(session).openapi()), so it cannot drift from the code; a running server serves the same document at /openapi.json and interactive docs at /docs.

Every state change goes through one route, POST /api/actions, whose body is one Action (a JSON object discriminated on its type). The Action schemas are on the Workbench Actions page; GET /api/actions returns the JSON schema of every Action the running session accepts, plugin Actions included. Reads are plain GETs and never recorded in the history.

docs.title: Events (GET /api/events)
docs.text:
The stream is Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream). It opens with a state event carrying the full session snapshot (the same payload as GET /api/state) and then carries every event the session publishes, each frame named by its type:

  • state — a fresh snapshot after any change (open, close, selection, settings, edits).
  • history — one recorded Action, in the shape GET /api/history lists.
  • job — a background job’s snapshot at each stage change (open, build, validate, save and Ollama pulls run as jobs; POST /api/actions answers 202 with the job and the outcome arrives here).
  • llm — provider and key status after a key is set or removed or a model pulled.
  • navigate — a map navigation request raised by a Navigate Action.

A : keepalive comment is sent after 15 seconds of silence so proxies keep the connection open; ?max_events=N closes the stream after N events, for scripts and tests.

docs.title: Local-bind guards
docs.text: On the default loopback bind the server answers 400 to any request whose Host header is not localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], and 403 to any state-changing request that names a foreign Origin or arrives Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site; see Explore in the Workbench for what that means when you expose the app.

docs.title: Plugin routes
docs.text: Each installed plugin’s router is mounted under /api/plugins/<id>/ and its static files under /plugins/<id>/. Those routes depend on what is installed, so they are not listed here; GET /api/plugins names the installed plugins and their state.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Read the session state, apply a no-argument Action, and watch one event from the stream. The server must be running (netstead app) on its default port.

curl http://127.0.0.1:8850/api/state
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8850/api/actions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"type": "clear_selection"}'
curl -N 'http://127.0.0.1:8850/api/events?max_events=1'

docs.title: Files in Specification
docs.text:
GMNS consists of a package of files as defined in the following table.

The following tables are automatically generated.

docs.title: General Modeling Network Specification (GMNS)
docs.text:
Name: gmns Version: 0.96 Homepage: https://github.com/zephyr-data-specs/GMNS

The General Modeling Network Specification (GMNS) defines a common machine (and human) readable format for sharing routable road network files. It is designed to be used in multi-modal static and dynamic transportation planning and operations models.

docs.title: link
docs.text:
A link is an edge in a network, defined by the nodes it travels from and to. It may have associated geometry information. Links have three types of attributes: - Those that define the physical location of the link (e.g., shape information, length, width) - Those that define the link’s directionality: from_node, to_node - Those that define properties in the direction of travel: capacity, free flow speed, number of lanes, permitted uses, grade, facility type

Primary key: link_id

Field Type Constraints Description link_id any required Primary key - could be SharedStreets Reference ID name string Optional. Street or Path Name from_node_id any required Required. Origin Node to_node_id any required Required. Destination Node directed boolean required Required. Whether the link is directed (travel only occurs from the from_node to the to_node) or undirected. geometry_id any Optional. Foreign key (Link_Geometry table). geometry any Optional. Link geometry, in well-known text (WKT) format. Optionally, other formats supported by geopandas (GeoJSON, PostGIS) may be used if specified in geometry_field_format in gmns.spec.json parent_link_id any Optional. The parent of this link. For example,for a sidewalk, this is the adjacent road. dir_flag integer enum=[1, -1, 0] Optional. 1 shapepoints go from from_node to to_node;-1 shapepoints go in the reverse direction;0 link is undirected or no geometry information is provided. length number min=0 Optional. Length of the link in long_length units grade number min=-100; max=100 % grade, negative is downhill facility_type string Facility type (e.g., freeway, arterial, etc.) capacity number min=0 Optional. Saturation capacity (passenger car equivalents / hr / lane) free_speed number min=0; max=200 Optional. Free flow speed, units defined by config file lanes integer min=0 Optional. Number of permanent lanes (not including turn pockets) in the direction of travel open to motor vehicles. It does not include bike lanes, shoulders or parking lanes. bike_facility string enum=[unseparated bike lane, buffered bike lane, separated bike lane, counter-flow bike lane, paved shoulder, shared lane, … (+4 more)] Optional. Type of bike facility along the link. ped_facility string enum=[unknown, none, shoulder, sidewalk, offstreet_path, crosswalk] Optional. Type of pedestrian accommodation along the link parking string enum=[unknown, none, parallel, angle, other] Optional. Type of parking along the link. allowed_uses string Optional. Set of allowed uses that should appear in either the use_definition or use_group tables; comma-separated. toll number Optional. Toll on the link, in currency units. jurisdiction string Optional. Owner/operator of the link. row_width number min=0 Optional. Width (short_length units) of the entire right-of-way (both directions).

Foreign keys:

  • from_node_id → node.node_id
  • to_node_id → node.node_id
  • geometry_id → geometry.geometry_id
  • parent_link_id → link.link_id

docs.title: node
docs.text:
A list of vertices that locate points on a map. Typically, they will represent intersections, but may also represent other points, such as a transition between divided and undivided highway. Nodes are the endpoints of a link (as opposed to the other type of vertex, location, which is used to represent points along a link)

Primary key: node_id

Field Type Constraints Description node_id any required Primary key name string x_coord number required Coordinate system specified in config file (longitude, UTM-easting etc.) y_coord number required Coordinate system specified in config file (latitude, UTM-northing etc.) z_coord number Optional. Altitude in short_length units. node_type string Optional. What it represents (intersection, transit station, park & ride). ctrl_type string enum=[no_control, yield, stop, stop_2_way, stop_4_way, signal_with_RTOR, … (+1 more)] Optional. Intersection control type. zone_id any Optional. Could be a Transportation Analysis Zone (TAZ) or city, or census tract, or census block. parent_node_id any Optional. Associated node. For example, if this node is a sidewalk, a parent_nodek_id could represent the intersection it is associated with.

Foreign keys:

  • zone_id → zone.zone_id
  • parent_node_id → node.node_id

docs.title: geometry
docs.text:
The geometry is an optional file that contains geometry information (shapepoints) for a line object. It is similar to Geometries in the SharedStreets reference system. The specification also allows for geometry information to be stored directly on the link table.

Primary key: geometry_id

Field Type Constraints Description geometry_id any required Primary key - could be SharedStreets Geometry ID geometry any Link geometry, in well-known text (WKT) format. Optionally, other formats supported by geopandas (GeoJSON, PostGIS) may be used if specified in geometry_field_format in gmns.spec.json.

docs.title: lane
docs.text:
The lane file allocates portions of the physical right-of-way that might be used for travel. It might be a travel lane, bike lane, or a parking lane. Lanes only are included in directed links; undirected links are assumed to have no lane controls or directionality. If a lane is added, dropped, or changes properties along the link, those changes are recorded on the segment_link table. Lanes are numbered sequentially, starting at either the centerline (two-way street) or the left shoulder (one-way street or divided highway with two centerlines).

Primary key: lane_id

Field Type Constraints Description lane_id any required Primary key link_id any required Required. Foreign key to link table. lane_num integer required; min=-10; max=10 Required. e.g., -1, 1, 2 (use left-to-right numbering). By convention, the left-most through lane is 1. Left-turn lanes have negative numbers allowed_uses string Optional. Set of allowed uses that should appear in either the use_definition or use_group tables; comma-separated. r_barrier string enum=[none, regulatory, physical] Optional. docs.title: link
docs.text:
A link is an edge in a network, defined by the nodes it travels from and to. It may have associated geometry information. Links have three types of attributes: - Those that define the physical location of the link (e.g., shape information, length, width) - Those that define the link’s directionality: from_node, to_node - Those that define properties in the direction of travel: capacity, free flow speed, number of lanes, permitted uses, grade, facility type

Primary key: link_id

Field Type Constraints Description link_id any required Primary key - could be SharedStreets Reference ID name string Optional. Street or Path Name from_node_id any required Required. Origin Node to_node_id any required Required. Destination Node directed boolean required Required. Whether the link is directed (travel only occurs from the from_node to the to_node) or undirected. geometry_id any Optional. Foreign key (Link_Geometry table). geometry any Optional. Link geometry, in well-known text (WKT) format. Optionally, other formats supported by geopandas (GeoJSON, PostGIS) may be used if specified in geometry_field_format in gmns.spec.json parent_link_id any Optional. The parent of this link. For example,for a sidewalk, this is the adjacent road. dir_flag integer enum=[1, -1, 0] Optional. 1 shapepoints go from from_node to to_node;-1 shapepoints go in the reverse direction;0 link is undirected or no geometry information is provided. length number min=0 Optional. Length of the link in long_length units grade number min=-100; max=100 % grade, negative is downhill facility_type string Facility type (e.g., freeway, arterial, etc.) capacity number min=0 Optional. Saturation capacity (passenger car equivalents / hr / lane) free_speed number min=0; max=200 Optional. Free flow speed, units defined by config file lanes integer min=0 Optional. docs.title: node
docs.text:
A list of vertices that locate points on a map. Typically, they will represent intersections, but may also represent other points, such as a transition between divided and undivided highway. Nodes are the endpoints of a link (as opposed to the other type of vertex, location, which is used to represent points along a link)

Primary key: node_id

What it represents (intersection, transit station, park & ride). ctrl_type string enum=[no_control, yield, stop, stop_2_way, stop_4_way, signal_with_RTOR, … (+1 more)] Optional. Intersection control type. zone_id any Optional. Could be a Transportation Analysis Zone (TAZ) or city, or census tract, or census block. parent_node_id any Optional. Associated node. docs.title: geometry
docs.text:
The geometry is an optional file that contains geometry information (shapepoints) for a line object. It is similar to Geometries in the SharedStreets reference system. The specification also allows for geometry information to be stored directly on the link table.

Primary key: geometry_id

Field Type Constraints Description geometry_id any required Primary key - could be SharedStreets Geometry ID geometry any Link geometry, in well-known text (WKT) format. Optionally, other formats supported by geopandas (GeoJSON, PostGIS) may be used if specified in geometry_field_format in gmns.spec.json.

docs.title: lane
docs.text:
The lane file allocates portions of the physical right-of-way that might be used for travel. It might be a travel lane, bike lane, or a parking lane. Lanes only are included in directed links; undirected links are assumed to have no lane controls or directionality. If a lane is added, dropped, or changes properties along the link, those changes are recorded on the segment_link table. Lanes are numbered sequentially, starting at either the centerline (two-way street) or the left shoulder (one-way street or divided highway with two centerlines).

Primary key: lane_id

Field Type Constraints Description lane_id any required Primary key link_id any required Required. Foreign key to link table. lane_num integer required; min=-10; max=10 Required. e.g., -1, 1, 2 (use left-to-right numbering). By convention, the left-most through lane is 1. Left-turn lanes have negative numbers allowed_uses string Optional. Set of allowed uses that should appear in either the use_definition or use_group tables; comma-separated. r_barrier string enum=[none, regulatory, physical] Optional. Whether a barrier exists to prevent vehicles from changing lanes to the right. l_barrier string enum=[none, regulatory, physical] Optional. Whether a barrier exists to prevent vehicles from changing lanes to the left width number min=0 Optional. Width of the lane, short_length units.

docs.title: location
docs.text:
A location is a vertex that is associated with a specific location along a link. Locations may be used to represent places where activities occur (e.g., driveways and bus stops). Its attributes are nearly the same as those for a node, except that the location includes an associated link and node, with location specified as distance along the link from the node.

Otherwise, link geometry is assumed to be a crow-fly distance from A node to B node. x_coord number Optional. Either provided, or derived from Link, Ref_Node and LR. y_coord number Optional.
